description:
The KCS emitted-telemetry (observability) extension — the clause a downstream conformance console has been shipping without.

VERIFIED AGAINST THE TEXT (2026-09-12, before this tasklist was authored).

KOINE HAS NEVER RECEIVED THIS. `grep -rn 'emitted-telemetry\|ObservedSpan'` over this repo matches NOTHING outside the roadmap row that records the gap. KCS's numbered sections run §1 Scope … §8 Prior art, so there is no §9 and no observability clause anywhere in it, while the console downstream shipped the vocabulary, declared its own tasklist gated on the ratified koine extension, and has reported SHIPPED AHEAD on every gate run since.

IT IS NOT ACADEMIC. koine's own ratification evidence is computed in part off that vocabulary: §5's control-plane predicates `cost_within_ceiling(invoke, budget)`, `tier_resolved(invoke, tier)` and `refused(step)` are asserted, in the cited live-run artifact, over frames carrying the emitted shape. So the shape is already load-bearing on this repo's evidence and is specified nowhere in it.

TWO HALVES, AND ONLY ONE OF THEM MAY STAY INFORMATIVE.
(1) AN OPTIONAL §9 — an exchange record (a `kind: "exchange"` frame carrying the verb, the capability, the two parties as KINP ids, world, tier, status, the ceiling AND ITS UNIT, actual spend, timings, and the ids the exchange touched). Emission stays OPTIONAL and a participant with no console is fully conformant — what is specified is OBSERVATION, not instrumentation.
(2) A §5 EVIDENCE-PRECEDENCE RULE, which cannot stay informative. It must say which decides `tier_resolved` / `cost_within_ceiling` / `refused` when a step carries BOTH an emitted record and an outcome the runner observed itself, and what happens when the two disagree. Without it two conformant runners choosing differently produce DIFFERENT CONFORMANCE REPORTS FROM ONE RUN — which is the same class of defect KCS §7 question 2's re-validation already found in `structure_matches` (delta R: its comparison basis is fixed nowhere, so two conformant runners may return different verdicts for one document).

A DATED PRIOR-ART SWEEP GATES THE FOLD. Span models and trace-context are mature standardised work, and `grep -rni 'opentelemetry\|traceparent\|trace-context'` over `specs/` returns NOTHING — this repo has never recorded reading them. Under the ADR-0006 / ADR-0010 discipline the choice is: profile by reference, or mint and record what was read and when. Taking the second without doing the first is what those ADRs exist to prevent.

VERSION. Minor, KCS 0.3.0 → 0.4.0: additive by section, but the precedence rule changes how existing §5 predicates evaluate, so it is not a patch.

THE SPLIT OF WORK. Ratifying is koine's; rewriting the console's span implementation against the folded text is the downstream implementer's. A draft with nine reconciliations (including un-denominated spend beside a grant that must denominate, and a `status` documented free-form but consumed as a closed enum) exists in that implementer's own tree and should be read as an input, not adopted as a decision.

userStories.title: The dated prior-art sweep, before a clause is written
userStories.description: ADR-0006/ADR-0010 discipline: profile by reference, or mint and record what was read and when. The sweep gates the fold.
acceptanceCriteria: A dated prior-art sweep is recorded covering the mature standardised work in this space — span/trace data models and trace-context propagation at minimum — saying WHAT was read, WHEN, and what each does and does not cover for an exchange record.

The verdict is explicit and is one of profile-by-reference or mint-and-record, with the reason stated. If anything is profiled by reference it is added to `docs/reference/upstream-standards.md` with its pin, so the drift check covers it like every other upstream.

The starting fact is recorded rather than assumed: no koine spec cites any of this prior art today (`grep -rni 'opentelemetry|traceparent|trace-context' specs/` returns nothing), so the sweep is a first reading and is dated as one.

The downstream draft and its nine reconciliations are read as INPUT and cited as a proposal, never adopted as a decision — and the implementer is referred to by ROLE, not by repository or product name, since this repo is public and its rows are role-scoped by design.

GATES: `node scripts/check-doc-integrity.mjs`, `node scripts/check-doc-links.mjs`, `node scripts/check-schemas.mjs`, `node scripts/check-registry.mjs`, `node scripts/check-tasklist-categories.mjs` and `bash scripts/check-roadmap-truth.sh` all green, with the observed output recorded.
userStories.notes: Sweep is docs/reference/kcs-telemetry-prior-art.md (236 lines), fetched LIVE on 2026-09-12 — not from memory: W3C Trace Context L1 (W3C Rec 2021-11-23, editorial update of the 2020-02-06 Rec), Trace Context L2 (CR Draft 2024-03-28), OpenTelemetry Spec 1.60.0 (Span fields + closed Status enum Unset/Ok/Error), the OTel trace SDK sampler (DROP/RECORD_ONLY/RECORD_AND_SAMPLE), semconv 1.44.0, the GenAI conventions (moved out, in-tree entries Deprecated, token counts only), CloudEvents v1.0.2. Starting fact recorded and re-measured: grep -rni 'opentelemetry|traceparent|trace-context' specs/ = 0 matches, repo-wide = 1 (the ROADMAP row). Verdict explicit and split: profile-by-reference for W3C Trace Context (correlation axis only), mint-and-record for the other 8 of the 11 record fields, OpenTelemetry resembled-not-adopted (no pin), CloudEvents dismissed with a re-open trigger. The one profiled upstream is now a row in docs/reference/upstream-standards.md with its pin, its row-provenance line and a review-log line scoped to what was actually fetched (1 row; the header's Last reviewed deliberately NOT moved, since no existing row was re-fetched). Entered state ⬜ not ✅ on purpose — it flips when KCS §9 cites it in US-2. Downstream draft cited as INPUT only, by ROLE ('conformance-console implementer'), never by repo/product; the 2 named reconciliations are recorded and the other 7 are explicitly NOT restated because they were not read. Indexed in docs/README.md. GATES, observed: doc-integrity OK (63 md files, 1967 relative links, all 3 status tables match) exit 0; doc-links 0 dead vs 0 on main exit 0; schemas OK (9 schemas, 278 positions, 80 $refs, 3 fixtures) exit 0; registry OK (31 relation names) exit 0; tasklist-categories OK exit 0; roadmap-truth coverage/stale/park all OK exit 0. userStories.title: An OPTIONAL §9 — the exchange record, specified as observation
userStories.description: Emission stays optional; what is specified is what an observer may rely on when a record IS emitted.
acceptanceCriteria: KCS gains a §9 specifying the exchange record: the verb, the capability, the two parties as KINP ids, world, tier, status, THE CEILING AND ITS UNIT, actual spend, timings, and the ids the exchange touched.

Emission is OPTIONAL and the text says so: a participant that emits nothing is fully conformant, consistent with KCB §4.3g. What §9 fixes is OBSERVATION — the shape an observer may rely on — not an obligation to instrument.

The two reconciliations the downstream draft flags as substantive are answered in the text rather than inherited: spend that is un-denominated beside a grant that MUST denominate its unit (KCB §5's refusal instrument for an unstated unit is the precedent), and a `status` documented free-form while consumed as a closed enum.

The record is expressed in terms the rest of the fabric already fixes — KINP ids for parties, KCB's `cost` shape and `budget_units` for the ceiling and the spend, KCB §4.2d frames where a frame is what carries it — and mints nothing a sibling spec already defines.
GATES: koine's six checks green, with observed output recorded.
userStories.notes: KCS 0.4.0 §9 added (lines 278-482 of specs/conformance-scenario.md, ~205 lines): clauses (a)-(i). (a) emission OPTIONAL in a NORMATIVE clause — a participant that emits nothing is fully conformant (KCB §4.3g's rule on this plane), argued from the sweep's load-bearing finding (OTel SDK's DROP sampling decision is conformant), so an absent record asserts nothing (KCB §4.5(c), §4.2b, KMI §2, KMI §7.1's reading). (b) the record: 12 named fields in a Presence/Value/Absent-reads table + a worked jsonc example using KINP §3.4 placeholder namespaces — kind (discriminator "exchange"), verb (KCB §4's five), capability ({name,version}, KCB §7.1's pair, 0.0.0-unknown), caller/callee (KINP ids), world (id or explicit null, absent != null), tier, status, ceiling {budget_units,unit,issuer?}, spend, started_at/ended_at (KGP §3.2's fixed UTC form), refs (typed by KINP §3.1 kind segment), trace (Trace Context trace-id/parent-id). Reconciliation 1 answered in (c): spend/ceiling denominate, same unit, no conversion; an un-denominated amount is NOT evidence for cost_within_ceiling and reads unstated, never within/zero — KCB §5's refuse-for-want-of-a-unit (MA-6) as the precedent. Reconciliation 2 answered in (d): status CLOSED at ok|refused|failed|unknown, detail only beside refused/failed (OTel Status' rule), absent+unrecognised both read unknown and MUST NOT be mapped. (e) borrows-not-mints list + the three-axes-called-tier disambiguation (provenance trust tier, never KGP §5's dialect tier, never KCB's free/paid cost.tier). (f) CARRIER NAMED — §4's observation log entry discriminated by kind, and the carrier KCS does not own (KCB §4.2d's single channel / §7.3g's single frame vocabulary) stated as not-specified-here, so §9 is not the ninth finding on ADR-0014's axis. (g) never-synthesized. (h) evidence precedence deferred to §5 (US-3). (i) what it does not do. Version moved 0.3.0 -> 0.4.0 with the three status mirrors (README.md, specs/README.md, ECOSYSTEM.md) + the specs/README.md prose count + CLAUDE.md's Current state bullet; §1 scope names §9; §2's example kcs_version -> 0.4.0; a Pressure test paragraph records §9 as published-not-exercised (DR-7's shape) with the single R count restated and unmoved. upstream-standards.md's W3C Trace Context row flipped ⬜ -> ✅ (KCS 0.4.0 §9(b)/(e) is the citing clause), and the sweep doc records the flip. GATES, observed: doc-integrity OK (63 md files, 2000 relative links, all 3 status tables match, conformance-scenario 0.4.0 candidate) exit 0; doc-links 0 dead vs 0 on main exit 0; schemas OK (9 schemas, 278 positions, 80 $refs, 3 fixtures) exit 0; registry OK (31 relation names) exit 0; tasklist-categories OK exit 0; roadmap-truth coverage/stale/park all OK exit 0. All six green.

userStories.title: The §5 evidence-precedence rule — the half that cannot stay informative
userStories.description: Two runners, one run, two reports is a defect in the gate itself. Fix it normatively.
acceptanceCriteria: §5 gains a NORMATIVE evidence-precedence rule saying which evidence decides `tier_resolved`, `cost_within_ceiling` and `refused` when a step carries BOTH an emitted record and an outcome the runner observed itself — and what a runner MUST do when the two disagree (a disagreement that is silently resolved is the failure mode; a disagreement that is reported is not).

The rule is written so that two conformant runners over ONE run produce the SAME verdict for each of those three predicates. That property is stated in the text as the thing the rule exists to guarantee.

The rule's interaction with KCS §7 question 1 is recorded: the fixed core versus declared console extensions, and the DR-10 drift finding that the downstream §5 vocabulary omits `structure_matches` and declares a predicate this spec names nowhere — a fixed core is only fixed if something checks it.

The version move is KCS 0.3.0 → 0.4.0 and the reasoning is stated: additive by section, but the precedence rule changes how EXISTING §5 predicates evaluate, so it is not a patch. All three status mirrors (`README.md`, `specs/README.md`, `ECOSYSTEM.md`) move with it, which `check-doc-integrity.mjs` enforces.

What the fold does NOT close is stated: KCS stays Candidate, delta R (`structure_matches`'s comparison basis) is untouched and still unowned, and the downstream re-write against the folded text is the implementer's work, not koine's. `docs/reference/promotability.md` is updated to match.
GATES: koine's six checks green, with observed output recorded.
userStories.notes: KCS §5.1 added (specs/conformance-scenario.md lines 142-283, ~142 lines): NORMATIVE evidence-precedence rule, clauses (a)-(g). The guaranteed property is stated FIRST in the text so a later revision can be measured against it: 'two conformant runners evaluating one run MUST reach the same verdict for each of these three predicates' (tier_resolved, cost_within_ceiling, refused). (a) two evidence kinds - a DIRECT OBSERVATION (a §4 step-2 log entry from a connection the runner opened itself) vs an ATTRIBUTED RECORD (§9, its emitter's assertion, §9g) - and the ordering: a direct observation OUTRANKS an attributed record ALWAYS, the reverse FORBIDDEN, argued from the sweep's load-bearing finding (this data is droppable by construction, so a record is a declaration not a measurement; evidence a subject authors by choosing what to emit is not evidence). (b) BINDING PRECEDES COMPARISON - bind on §9(b)'s stated facts (verb/capability/caller/callee/trace/refs), MUST NOT bind on timing proximity or log adjacency, because two runners binding different records diverge before the ordering is ever reached. (c) a six-row exhaustive case table (MUST decide exactly so, MUST NOT apply any other rule). (d) A DISAGREEMENT IS REPORTED, NEVER RESOLVED: MUST NOT silently prefer either, MUST fail the assertion, MUST carry BOTH readings named by evidence kind and (for a record) emitter KINP id; reasoned - the ordering fixes which account the runner reports as its own finding and does not make a contradiction disappear, and §4's report being content-addressed makes a silently resolved divergence REPRODUCIBLY invisible, which is how delta R's divergence hides. Mints NO new report verdict (a disagreement is a fail, §4's pass/fail shape unchanged). (e) what a disagreement IS: on the predicate's own fact never the whole record, per-predicate comparison facts spelled out (failed != refused in §9d's closed enum; spend measured in the ceiling's stated unit, nothing converted; tier is §9(e)'s provenance trust tier and another axis's token is a NON-CONFORMANT RECORD not a disagreement); AN ABSENCE IS NEVER A DISAGREEMENT (MUST NOT default an unstated tier/ceiling/un-denominated amount into a comparison, MUST NOT read un-denominated as 'within'); several records are ATTRIBUTIONS NEVER MERGED (ADR-0014 on this plane). (f) §7 question 1 interaction recorded, and it makes the question LARGER not smaller: §5.1 is fixed-core surface a NAME check cannot see - two runners may agree on every predicate name, reject the same unknowns, and still return different reports, because the evidence rule appears NOWHERE in a scenario document (§2 declares kcs_version and no evidence profile; §5.1 adds no field to change that); DR-10's drift (downstream vocabulary omits structure_matches, declares media_map_complete koine names nowhere, hardcoded count of 18 names as the check) is quoted as the evidence; declared console extensions (V-8, MA-11) are bound by (a)'s ordering and declare their evidence rule beside the predicate; §5's fixed core otherwise unchanged, no predicate added/removed/re-signatured, delta R UNTOUCHED. (g) what it does not do. VERSION REASONING stated in the text and the changelog: MINOR not patch, and the decisive fact is the LAST ROW of (c) - a predicate with NEITHER an observation NOR a bound record now FAILS, where before a cost_within_ceiling could be read as passing because nothing refused the invoke; that is the fail-open inversion KCB §4.4c ('highest published') and KMI §7.1 (unreachable store) refuse by name, so closing it NARROWS how a conformant runner may evaluate. 0.4.0 header was already published in US-2 and all three CI-checked mirrors (README.md, specs/README.md, ECOSYSTEM.md) already carry it - re-verified green by check-doc-integrity; each mirror's DESCRIPTION cell extended to name §5.1. Also edited: §1 Scope names §5.1; §9(h) sharpened from a stub into a pointer at the actual rule with its three load-bearing clauses and the two consequences that land back on §9; §7 question 1 gains the larger-not-smaller paragraph; Pressure test retitled to cover BOTH new sections as PUBLISHED-NOT-EXERCISED, with §5.1 named the sharper case (a rule about divergence BETWEEN TWO RUNNERS and the fabric has one, so a green run from that runner is internally consistent by construction and cannot falsify it - the same property that made delta R unfindable by replay; what would exercise it is a leg putting a record and an observation in disagreement on purpose, and no scenarios/ document does); the 0.4.0 changelog entry EXTENDED (not a second entry) with the §5.1 half, the minor-not-patch reasoning and the closes-nothing paragraph. WHAT IT DOES NOT CLOSE, stated in four places (spec, changelog, promotability.md, CLAUDE.md): KCS stays Candidate; delta R untouched and still unowned - R is a COMPARISON basis and §5.1 an EVIDENCE basis, same class of defect on two axes, and supplying one supplies nothing to the other; DR-10 still downstream under ADR-0001 and unowned; the re-write against the folded text is the implementer's. docs/reference/promotability.md updated in both places (the KCS row and item 2 of the ranking narrative). CLAUDE.md's Current state KCS bullet (the fourth mirror, unchecked by CI) extended. The sweep doc records where its §3.1 finding landed and which two points it did NOT settle. GATES, observed: doc-integrity OK (63 md files, 2008 relative links, all 3 status tables match, conformance-scenario 0.4.0 candidate) exit 0; doc-links 0 dead vs 0 on main exit 0; schemas OK (9 schemas, 278 positions, 80 $refs, 3 fixtures) exit 0; registry OK (31 relation names) exit 0; tasklist-categories OK (1 categorized) exit 0; roadmap-truth coverage OK (61 completed named) / stale OK (51 checked, 1 allowlisted) / park OK, exit 0. All six green.
